author: Vox
description:
There was a lot of talk about communism on the campaign trail for the 2026 midterm elections. Trump and the right worked to convince voters that candidates associated with the Democratic Socialists of America — and by extension the entire Democratic Party — had communist tendencies. 

As 2026 midterm votes are still being counted, DSA candidates have had a strong showing across the country, capturing electoral victories in several states. The Gen Z historian Kahlil Greene (@historycanthide)  explores the policies and ideas the DSA supports, and how it differs from the Communist Party of the USA (CPUSA) in the newest episode of our series, Kahlil, Explains.

title: The right’s attempts at a new Red Scare

author: Vox
description:
There’s been a lot of “communist” talk on the midterms campaign trail. It’s become Trump’s favorite new perceived threat coming from the left. But it’s actually not new at all. 

US politicians, especially on the right, have long described communism as a threat to the American way of life. As a result, the United States has undergone historical periods of intense and occasionally violent means to suppress the spread of communism. Beyond the clash between capitalism and communism as economic systems, a line is often drawn between communist ideology and religion in America, specifically Christianity. 

In the 1950s, President Dwight D. Eisenhower added the words “Under God” to the Pledge of Allegiance, doubling down on the Christian values of an anti-communist America. The phrase “In God We Trust” was also added to US currency.
